title: Trade buyer spend budget, period and reservation/commitment ledger
description: ADR-SHARED-042 section 14, Decision 5 (Platform Owner, 2026-10-22): cumulative buyer spending authority. Trade owns this commercial spending-control ledger; ERP remains the accounting authority and Payments the funds-movement authority. Consumption is authorised purchasing commitment, never cash or invoice settlement. Every applicable ceiling must pass independently: the per-transaction limit (trade SpendLimit, unchanged), the mandatory calendar-month MEMBERSHIP budget, and any configured AGREEMENT or ORGANISATION budget. No role may disregard a cumulative budget, and approving one purchase never raises a budget. Available capacity is limit minus committed minus active reservations. A formally submitted purchase reserves its full amount; the reservation is held through approval, converted atomically to committed consumption at order commit (never counted twice), and released only through a verified lifecycle transition. Refunds, returns and historical adjustments never restore capacity without a separately approved reversal policy. This contract activates nothing.

timezone.description: IANA time zone governing period boundaries. UTC is the baseline unless the approved policy states another zone.

agreementReference.description: The procurement agreement or contract the budget is bound to, as Trade's commercial terms record it.

budgetScope.description: MEMBERSHIP: one member's mandatory calendar-month budget. AGREEMENT: the ceiling of one procurement agreement over its term, binding when configured. ORGANISATION: a calendar-month budget shared by every purchasing member of the buyer Organisation, binding when configured.

periodKind.description: CALENDAR_MONTH is the standard period, never a rolling interval. AGREEMENT_TERM is the agreement's own bounded term.

BudgetPeriod.description: One concrete period: starts_at inclusive, ends_at exclusive. For CALENDAR_MONTH both are local midnights of the first day of consecutive months in the governing time zone (scripts/tests/test_buyer_spend_budget.py checks this; JSON Schema cannot).

BuyerSpendBudgetPolicy.description: A versioned budget policy. Its revision is monotonic; any change to limit, scope, period or effective interval is a new revision, and reservations or approvals bound to an earlier revision must be revalidated.

market_id.description: The canonical CP Market. A Trade market_key is usable only through a governed, exact mapping.

limit_minor.description: Never null, zero or inferred: an absent budget is SPEND_POLICY_NOT_CONFIGURED, never unlimited.

ledgerEntryKind.description: RESERVE acquires capacity for a reservation (at formal submission, or additional capacity when the amount increases). COMMIT converts reserved capacity into committed consumption at order commit; it never adds consumption. RELEASE returns the verified unused portion of a reservation (rejection, cancellation, expiry, reduction, period rollover).

SpendLedgerEntry.description: One append-only ledger entry against one budget policy revision and period. Entries are never updated or deleted. A reservation is bound to one immutable purchase and is never transferred between buyers, Markets, currencies, policies or periods. The idempotency key makes a retried command return the original entry instead of a second one.

commitment_reference.description: The committed order, required for COMMIT.

actor_principal_id.description: The CP canonical Principal whose governed action produced the entry (buyer, approver or the lifecycle owner).

BudgetCapacity.description: The balance of one policy revision and period: available_minor = limit_minor - committed_minor - reserved_minor, never negative.
